display.purpose: Hero titles only. Libre Baskerville, fluid clamp.

body.purpose: All running text. Weight 300 for descriptions, 400 default.

eyebrow.purpose: Section kickers in copper, 0.15em tracking, uppercase.

body-sm.purpose: Secondary running text and empty-state copy. 0.9375rem.

small.purpose: Table cells, meta lines, signal labels. 0.875rem.

caption.purpose: Notes, DIDs, inline errors under controls. 0.75rem.

stat.purpose: The account handle on the detail page. Libre Baskerville 1.875rem.

shadows.name: featured-glow
shadows.purpose: Copper halo under featured and CTA cards. Atmosphere, not rank.

shadows.name: hover-lift
shadows.purpose: Paired with translateY(-2px..-4px) on interactive surfaces.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Input focus. A ring, not a flash.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Subtle color and border hover transitions.

motion.name: emerge
motion.purpose: Above-fold entrance. Stagger children 0.05s-0.1s, fill backwards when delayed.

motion.name: scroll-reveal
motion.purpose: Below-fold sections via IntersectionObserver at threshold 0.15, rootMargin 0px 0px -50px 0px.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: Ambient background orbs. Must stay barely perceptible.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The amber-to-copper call to action. The one place ground color becomes foreground.
components.css: .ds-btn-primary { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1.0625rem; font-weight: 500; color: #0c0a09; background: linear-gradient(135deg, #f59e0b 0%, #c9956c 100%); border: none; border-radius: 12px; padding: 1rem 2rem; cursor: pointer; box-shadow: 0 4px 20px -4px rgba(245,158,11,0.4); transition: all 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: translateY(-3px); box-shadow: 0 8px 30px -4px rgba(245,158,11,0.5); } .ds-btn-primary:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(201,149,108,0.4); } .ds-btn-primary:active { transform: translateY(0); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn-primary { transition: none; } .ds-btn-primary:hover { transform: none; } }

components.name: Ghost Button
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 500; color: #d6d3d1; background: transparent; border: 1px solid rgba(168,162,158,0.2); border-radius: 8px; padding: 0.625rem 1.25rem; cursor: pointer; transition: all 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: #fffbeb; border-color: rgba(201,149,108,0.4); background: rgba(201,149,108,0.1); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(201,149,108,0.15); } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-btn-ghost { transition: none; } }

components.name: Standard Card
components.description: The default surface. Flat at rest, lifts when touched.
components.html:
Amplification detected

Three accounts quoted your post in the last day.
components.css: .ds-card { background: linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(41,37,36,0.4) 0%, rgba(28,25,23,0.5) 100%); border: 1px solid rgba(168,162,158,0.08); border-radius: 16px; padding: 2rem; transition: all 0.4s cubic-bezier(0.16,1,0.3,1); } .ds-card:hover { border-color: rgba(201,149,108,0.2); transform: translateY(-2px); box-shadow: 0 20px 40px -10px rgba(0,0,0,0.4); } .ds-card-title { font-family: 'Libre Baskerville', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: 1.25rem; line-height: 1.3; color: #fffbeb; margin: 0 0 0.5rem; } .ds-card-body { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 300; font-size: 1rem; line-height: 1.65; color: #a8a29e; margin: 0; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-card { transition: none; } .ds-card:hover { transform: none; } }

components.name: Featured Card
components.description: The highest-rank surface. Tone ranks it; the copper glow is atmosphere.
components.html:
Keeping watch

Charcoal scores accounts before they reach you.
components.css: .ds-card-featured { background: linear-gradient(145deg, rgba(41,37,36,0.7) 0%, rgba(28,25,23,0.8) 100%); border: 1px solid rgba(168,162,158,0.15); border-radius: 24px; padding: 3rem; box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(0,0,0,0.25), 0 20px 50px -10px rgba(0,0,0,0.5), 0 0 80px -20px rgba(201,149,108,0.3); } .ds-card-featured-title { font-family: 'Libre Baskerville', Georgia, serif; font-weight: 400; font-size: clamp(1.75rem, 4vw, 2.5rem); line-height: 1.1; color: #fffbeb; margin: 0 0 0.75rem; } .ds-card-featured-body { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-weight: 300; font-size: 1.125rem; line-height: 1.65; color: #a8a29e; margin: 0; }

components.name: Text Input
components.description: Container-wrapped field with a copper focus ring and an @ prefix that warms on focus.
components.html: @
components.css: .ds-input-label { display: block; font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8125rem; font-weight: 500; color: #d6d3d1; letter-spacing: 0.03em; text-transform: uppercase; margin-bottom: 0.625rem; } .ds-input-wrap { display: flex; align-items: center; background: rgba(12,10,9,0.6); border: 1px solid rgba(168,162,158,0.15); border-radius: 12px; padding: 0 1rem; transition: all 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input-wrap:focus-within { border-color: #c9956c; background: rgba(12,10,9,0.8); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(201,149,108,0.15); } .ds-input-prefix { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; color: #78716c; transition: color 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-input-wrap:focus-within .ds-input-prefix { color: #c9956c; } .ds-input { flex: 1; border: none; background: transparent; padding: 1rem 0 1rem 0.25rem; font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 1rem; font-weight: 400; color: #fef3c7; outline: none; } .ds-input::placeholder { color: #57534e; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-input-wrap, .ds-input-prefix { transition: none; } }

components.name: Threat Tier Badge
components.description: Signature component. Colored TEXT, not a filled chip — no fill, border or radius. Severity lives here and nowhere else, always desaturated. Measures 7.8-13.7:1 on the ground.
components.html: High Elevated Watch Low
components.css: .ds-tier { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; margin-right: 0.75rem; } .ds-tier-high { color: #fca5a5; } .ds-tier-elevated { color: #fdba74; } .ds-tier-watch { color: #fcd34d; } .ds-tier-low { color: #a8a29e; }

components.name: Abstention Badge
components.description: No reading was taken. Deliberately outside the tier scale, but staying in the text idiom — Muted with a dashed underline, never a filled chip. TARGET STATE: today a null tier renders in Low's exact color (#245).
components.css: .ds-tier-abstained { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.875rem; font-weight: 500; color: #78716c; text-decoration: underline dashed rgba(168,162,158,0.45); text-underline-offset: 4px; }

components.name: Brand Mark
components.description: Concentric rings reading as absorption and as a sweep. Rings pulse, core breathes.
components.css: .ds-mark { display: inline-block; width: 72px; height: 72px; color: #c9956c; } .ds-mark svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; } /* Rings pulse and the core breathes on one 4.5s cycle, the rings staggered 0.4s apart. transform-box/transform-origin scale each circle about its own centre rather than the SVG's 0,0 corner. Base opacity moves to a custom property so the keyframe can lift it by a relative +0.2 instead of flattening all five rings to one absolute value. */ .ds-mark svg circle { transform-box: fill-box; transform-origin: center; opacity: var(--ds-ring-opacity); animation: ds-mark-pulse 4.5s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1) infinite; } .ds-mark svg circle:nth-child(1) { --ds-ring-opacity: 0.15; animation-delay: 0s; } .ds-mark svg circle:nth-child(2) { --ds-ring-opacity: 0.25; animation-delay: 0.4s; } .ds-mark svg circle:nth-child(3) { --ds-ring-opacity: 0.35; animation-delay: 0.8s; } .ds-mark svg circle:nth-child(4) { --ds-ring-opacity: 0.5; animation-delay: 1.2s; } .ds-mark svg circle:nth-child(5) { --ds-ring-opacity: 0.7; animation-delay: 1.6s; } .ds-mark svg circle:nth-child(6) { --ds-ring-opacity: 1; animation-name: ds-mark-breathe; animation-delay: 0s; } @keyframes ds-mark-pulse { 0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); opacity: var(--ds-ring-opacity); } 50% { transform: scale(1.03); opacity: calc(var(--ds-ring-opacity) + 0.2); } } @keyframes ds-mark-breathe { 0%, 100% { transform: scale(1); } 50% { transform: scale(1.02); } } /* Now disables a real animation: the rings hold the base opacity from the rule above and stop moving. */ @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-mark svg circle { animation: none; } }

components.name: Navigation
components.description: Fixed over a gradient fade rather than a solid bar, so the ground stays continuous.
components.html: How it worksSign in
components.css: /* Fixed to the top, as the description says and as the shipped nav does: without position and offsets it sits in normal flow and the gradient fade has nothing to fade over. z-index 100 matches the app's own nav, so page content and hero backdrops pass beneath it. */ .ds-nav { position: fixed; top: 0; left: 0; right: 0; z-index: 100; display: flex; align-items: center; gap: 2rem; padding: 1.5rem 2rem; background: linear-gradient(to bottom, rgba(12,10,9,0.8) 0%, transparent 100%); } .ds-nav-brand { display: inline-block; width: 36px; height: 36px; color: #c9956c; margin-right: auto; } .ds-nav-brand svg { width: 100%; height: 100%; } .ds-nav-link { font-family: Outfit, system-ui, sans-serif; font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 500; color: #d6d3d1; text-decoration: none; transition: color 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.4,0,0.2,1); } .ds-nav-link:hover { color: #fffbeb; } .ds-nav-link:focus-visible { outline: none; box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(201,149,108,0.15); border-radius: 4px; } @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) { .ds-nav-link { transition: none; } }

narrative.overview:
Someone is awake, watching the door, and the fire is still lit. Charcoal names accounts likely to harass the person using it — subject matter that pulls hard toward the security-console idiom of neon-on-black, red alert bars and dense telemetry. This system refuses that pull deliberately. The ground is a warm near-black, the text is cream rather than white, the accents are copper and amber, and the threat tiers are desaturated so that even a High finding is legible rather than alarming.

The warmth is not decoration; it is the argument. The product name evokes activated charcoal absorbing toxins, and the concentric-ring mark reads as absorption and as a sweep at once. What remains after the harmful content is filtered is supposed to feel like calm, so the interface behaves like a lit room rather than an operations center. Depth is atmospheric and layered — a base gradient, warmth radials, and slow drifting orbs, all of it barely perceptible and none of it competing with the reading.

Components behave as calm instruments: precise, unhurried, responsive without demanding. The interface never raises its voice, even when the finding is High. That restraint is what makes the findings credible — a system that shouts about everything cannot be trusted when something is genuinely wrong.
keyCharacteristics: Warm near-black ground (#0c0a09); never pure black, never pure white text
Serif display (Libre Baskerville) against geometric sans body (Outfit)
Copper as the single recurring accent; amber reserved for action
Desaturated threat tiers — soft red, not alarm red
Atmosphere from layered gradients and 25–30s ambient drift, never from chrome
Motion that reveals, never bounces; prefers-reduced-motion honored throughout

rules.name: The No-Pure Rule
rules.body: Never #fff for text and never #000 for background. Cream (#fffbeb / #fef3c7) and Night Ground (#0c0a09) are the extremes. Pure values break the warmth that the entire identity rests on.

rules.name: The Copper-Is-Not-Status Rule
rules.body: Copper marks identity and attention. Amber marks action. Neither ever encodes severity — severity belongs exclusively to the tier scale. A copper badge implying danger is a defect.

rules.name: The Indoor Voice Rule
rules.body: Threat tiers stay desaturated at all times. A High finding is #fca5a5, not #ef4444. The system reports; it does not shout. Saturating a tier to increase urgency is the single fastest way to make this product feel like the thing it was built not to be.

rules.name: The Border Rule
rules.body: Borders are rgba(168, 162, 158, …) at 0.08–0.2 opacity at rest, shifting toward rgba(201, 149, 108, 0.2–0.4) on hover. Borders are how surfaces separate; contrast is not.

rules.name: The Serif-Heads-Only Rule
rules.body: Libre Baskerville is for headings, section titles, quotes, and the brand name. It never sets body copy, navigation, buttons, or form fields. Outfit never sets a heading.

rules.name: The Italic Accent Rule
rules.body: The emphasized word in a hero heading takes font-style: italic and Reading Copper. One word per heading — the device stops working the moment it repeats.

rules.name: The Tone-Ranks Rule
rules.body: If a surface needs to read as more important, raise its background and border opacity — do not give it a shadow. Shadows that encode rank collide with shadows that encode state, and the interface stops being readable at a glance.

rules.name: The Barely-There Rule
rules.body: Background warmth exists to create atmosphere, never to attract attention. If a reviewer notices the orbs before the content, the layer is too strong.

dos: Do use Cream for text and Night Ground for backgrounds. The No-Pure Rule is absolute.
Do keep severity in the tier chip and nowhere else. Copper is identity, amber is action.
Do rank surfaces with tone — background and border opacity — and reserve shadow for interaction.
Do set every heading in Libre Baskerville and everything else in Outfit.
Do ship prefers-reduced-motion handling with any animated surface. It is mandatory, not a nicety, for an audience often reading this while distressed.
Do render abstention outside the tier scale, as an outlined chip.
Do mark every decorative layer aria-hidden="true".
donts: Don't saturate a threat tier to convey urgency. The Indoor Voice Rule is the difference between this product and the console it refuses to be.

Don't build anything that reads as a security operations console (neon-on-black, red alert banners, monospace-everything, telemetry chrome), a generic SaaS dashboard (white cards, Inter everywhere, blue primary, purple gradient hero), clinical or medical (cool grays, hard edges, chart-first), or a playful consumer app (bounce easing, mascots, confetti, emoji-as-status). All four are confirmed anti-references.
Don't use amber outside a call to action, or copper to indicate state.
Don't give a surface a resting shadow to make it feel important.
Don't let the ambient background become noticeable.
Don't repeat the italic copper accent more than once per heading.
Don't square a corner. Nothing in this system has a hard 90-degree edge.
